open_obligations: Do not equate worst-case ASD with worst-case correctness in Brown-Cohen et al.'s sense.
Check whether either paper defines worst-case over inputs, over agents, or both.
Check whether Brown-Cohen et al.'s lower-bound question bears on worst-case ASD.
in.other_title: Limitation: average-case guarantees only; judge payoff imperfectly tracks correctness
in.rationale: Sudhir et al. propose looking at worst-case rather than average-case ASD as an important direction, because superhuman oversight must prevent rare catastrophic actions. Brown-Cohen et al. state prover-estimator debate's guarantees are average-case only and the judge's payoff imperfectly tracks correctness, but say they believe such an average-case analysis is necessary and call formalising this an open question; one is an empirical benchmark metric, the other a complexity-theoretic guarantee.
in.scope: proposed SAME_QUESTION_DIFFERENT_SETTING: whether oversight protocols should be analysed or measured in the average case or in the worst case, for a complexity-theoretic debate guarantee and for a benchmark metric (ASD)

text: The authors name as an important direction measuring worst-case rather than average-case ASD, since superhuman AI oversight must prevent rare catastrophic actions (e.g. one piece of vulnerable code enabling weight exfiltration), and suggest protocols that raise worst-case ASD should be more robust to such failures.
title: Do protocols that raise worst-case ASD resist rare catastrophic failures?
